response: The internet began as a U.S. Department of Defense research project in the 1960s, with ARPANET’s first message in 1969, and evolved into a global network after the 1983 adoption of TCP/IP protocols. Key milestones like Tim Berners-Lee’s World Wide Web (1989), the Mosaic browser (1993), and the dot-com boom—whose survivors include Amazon and Google—brought the web to the public, while the mid-2000s rise of social media, the 2007 iPhone, and cloud services like AWS (2006) made it mobile and pervasive. Today, it connects over 5 billion people and underpins virtually every aspect of modern life, from commerce to communication to entertainment.
